title: Panegyricus in Origenem: Gregory's thanksgiving to his teacher Origen
pass_a_gloss: Panegyric Oration and Thanksgiving to Origen (Oratio Panegyrica et Charisteria). Gregory Thaumaturgus, as a young student, delivers this oration of thanksgiving to his teacher Origen upon completing five years of study under him at Caesarea in Palestine. The oration is both a eulogy and a profession of gratitude. Gregory begins with an exordium on the difficulty of praising a great man. He acknowledges his youth and inexperience but is compelled by gratitude. He traces his journey: born in Neocaesarea, lost father at age 14, studied law at Berytus, met Origen at Caesarea, studied under him for five years, converted to Christianity. He praises Origen's encyclopedic learning: dialectic, geometry, arithmetic, music, grammar, rhetoric, all philosophies. Origen turned students from secular learning to Christian faith. Gregory credits Origen with his conversion. The oration ends with a doxology: praise to God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Jerome and Theodoret testify to this oration's existence and quality.
source_ref: Opera Omnia (Migne PG 10), Panegyricus in Origenem (lines ~9085-13185)
notes_covered: Delivered at Caesarea in Palestine after 5 years of study under Origen
Gregory was ~15-20 years old at the time
Jerome (De Viris Illustribus) and Theodoret testify to this oration
Vossius notes reference Demosthenes, Plato, Socrates, Bernard of Clairvaux
